name: Question 13
problem: At which points on the curve ${y}^{2}-4xy=-5{x}^{2}+1$ is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector $i?$
worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-4xy & =-5{x}^{2}+1 \\ {y}^{2}-4xy+5{x}^{2} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)={y}^{2}-4xy+5{x}^{2}$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=1.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows:

$$
t(x,y)={f}_{y}(x,y)\,i-{f}_{x}(x,y)\,j
$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & ={f}_{y}(x,y)\,i-{f}_{x}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}-4xy+5{x}^{2})i-\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}-4xy+5{x}^{2})j \\  & =2(y-2x)\,i-(10x-4y)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to $i$, we must have $t\cdot i=0.$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y)\cdot i & =0 \\ (2(y-2x)\,i-(10x-4y)\,j)\cdot i & =0 \\ 2(y-2x) & =0 \\ y & =2x\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $y=2x$ into the equation of our curve gives:  

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-4xy+5{x}^{2} & =1 \\ (2x)^{2}-4x(2x)+5{x}^{2} & =1 \\ 4{x}^{2}-8{x}^{2}+5{x}^{2} & =1 \\ {x}^{2} & =1 \\ x & =\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally:

- If $x=1$, we get $y=2$ and the corresponding point is $(1,2).$

- If $x=-1$, we get $y=-2$ and the corresponding point is $(-1,-2).$

Question 13
?

At which points on the curve y2−4xy=−5x2+1 is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector i?

a
(1,3) and (3,−2)
b
(−1,2) and (1,−2)
c
(1,2) and (−1,−2)
d
(3,2) and (−1,3)
e
(1,1) and (−1,−1)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we bring all variables to one side: y2−4xy=−5x2+1y2−4xy+5x2=1

If we set f(x,y)=y2−4xy+5x2, our curve can be viewed as the level curve f(x,y)=1.

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows: t(x,y)=fy(x,y)i−fx(x,y)j

So, we calculate t(x,y):

t(x,y)=fy(x,y)i−fx(x,y)j=∂∂y(y2−4xy+5x2)i−∂∂x(y2−4xy+5x2)j=2(y−2x)i−(10x−4y)j

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to i, we must have t⋅i=0.

t(x,y)⋅i=0(2(y−2x)i−(10x−4y)j)⋅i=02(y−2x)=0y=2x

Substituting y=2x into the equation of our curve gives:

y2−4xy+5x2=1(2x)2−4x(2x)+5x2=14x2−8x2+5x2=1x2=1x=±1

Finally:

  • If x=1, we get y=2 and the corresponding point is (1,2).

  • If x=−1, we get y=−2 and the corresponding point is (−1,−2).
